claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureEffect::modify_roll_advantage
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Reckless Attack grants Advantage on the barbarian's own Strength-based attack rolls. The v4 atom modify_roll_advantage exists and is used in MasteryEffect, but ClassFeatureEffect only allows grant_extra_action and heal_hp. A new variant for class-feature-initiated roll-advantage effects is needed.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Doing so gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureEffect::grant_advantage_on_attacks_against_self (detrimental self-rider)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The symmetric penalty of Reckless Attack gives incoming attackers Advantage against the barbarian. No existing ClassFeatureEffect variant models 'attack rolls targeting self gain advantage'. This is a distinct effect polarity (self-as-defender) not covered by modify_roll_advantage (self-as-attacker) or any other current effect type.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time

claude_proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap::unlimited
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Reckless Attack has no use-count limit — it may be triggered every turn with no rest reset. ClassFeatureActivationMechanics requires a UseCountResource whose cap must be either fixed or threshold_tiers; there is no 'unlimited' or 'no resource' variant.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. [No frequency restriction stated in the text.]

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureActivationMechanics::duration (turn-scoped expiry)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Reckless Attack creates effects that persist 'until the start of your next turn' — a timed lifecycle unlike the one-shot instantaneous effects of Action Surge or Second Wind. ClassFeatureActivationMechanics has no duration or expiry field; adding one (or a new turn-scoped expiry variant) is needed to model temporary-state class features.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: gives you Advantage on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have Advantage during that time
